Quarterly revenue grew by twelve percent year over year, beating internal forecast and street consensus by a comfortable margin and reaching a new all-time high for the company while compounding on the strong year ago period.
Customer churn dropped to its lowest level in two years across all market segments and product lines, with enterprise retention reaching a record high, mid-market churn down by half, and small-business churn improving for the third consecutive quarter.
Three new enterprise accounts signed during the period with multi-year commitments, expanding the named-account roster into two new verticals and unlocking incremental services attach opportunities for next year while raising average contract value across the segment.
Gross margin expanded by two hundred basis points on improved infrastructure costs, lower third-party data licensing fees, disciplined hosting renegotiations, a one-time true-up on prior-period accruals, and the ramp of a more favorable product mix.
Product engineering shipped four major feature releases across the platform this quarter, including the long-awaited collaboration suite, the new mobile experience, the analytics rebuild, a series of small but high-impact ergonomic improvements, and a new public application programming interface.
Operating expenses came in below plan despite continued investment in headcount and go-to-market, with disciplined spend management throughout the organization, a deliberate slowing of non-essential travel and consulting engagements, and tighter governance on new vendor contracts.
Sales pipeline coverage exiting the quarter sits comfortably above three times the next-quarter target with a healthier mid-funnel mix than a year ago and a marked increase in deals sourced by the partner channel and the customer success organization.
Net dollar retention crossed one hundred and twenty percent for the first time, reflecting both expansion within existing accounts and reduced contraction across the install base, with the largest cohort gains in financial services, healthcare, and the public sector.
Cash from operations turned solidly positive for the first time in eight quarters, supported by improved collections, more disciplined working capital management, the timing of certain large customer prepayments, and a thoughtful approach to capital expenditure phasing.
Hiring plans for the remainder of the year remain on track with offer-accept rates above benchmark and an unusually deep bench of internal candidates progressing toward senior leadership roles in engineering, product, customer success, and the global sales organization.
Customer satisfaction scores set a new high water mark, with both Net Promoter Score and customer satisfaction measurements showing improvement against the prior quarter and the full prior year on a like-for-like basis, with significant improvement among recently launched product lines.
International expansion progressed in line with the plan, with the EMEA region now contributing roughly one quarter of new logo bookings and APAC pipeline beginning to mature into late-stage opportunities, supported by a deliberate localization investment.
Marketing efficiency improved measurably as paid acquisition costs declined and content engagement metrics climbed, helped by a refresh of the corporate brand system, a new analyst relations program, and a more focused approach to events and field marketing motion.
Risk and compliance posture strengthened with the completion of a major security audit, the expansion of the privacy program into three new jurisdictions, and the closure of all priority one and priority two findings from the prior year audit cycle on schedule.
Strategic partnerships closed in the quarter unlock new distribution surface and integrate the platform more deeply with the broader ecosystem, with several joint go-to-market commitments queued up for execution in the first half of the following fiscal year.
Capital allocation framework continues to balance growth, profitability, and balance-sheet resilience, with management remaining disciplined about the timing and pace of additional investment while preserving optionality for opportunistic transactions and accretive acquisitions.
Talent and culture initiatives advanced on multiple fronts, including the rollout of a refreshed performance management system, expanded benefits in three regions, two flagship internal mobility programs, and a strengthened mentorship and learning organization.
Looking ahead to the next quarter, management expects continued momentum across the core business, accelerating contribution from recently launched products, additional gross margin tailwinds, and disciplined operating expense growth that should drive further operating leverage.
